prompts.text: A parrot learns one phrase from every person in our group. Which phrase causes the most trouble?
Which friend would take an unusually confident pigeon as a personal challenge?
Our group volunteering at a puppy adoption event or trying to photograph squirrels without disturbing them?
A cat walking across the board game is a better excuse for losing than anything a person could invent.
Tell me about an animal interrupting a perfectly serious conversation at exactly the wrong moment.
People who insist they dislike pets sometimes have the most detailed opinions about someone else's dog.
Which friend would secretly spend a holiday feeding every stray cat on the street?
A tiny dog steals the picnic blanket we're sitting on. Who negotiates with it?
Giving imaginary job titles to zoo animals or creating a backstory for the neighbour's mysterious cat?
If a bird starts copying our laughter, we should probably accept it as an honorary friend.
What kind of costume would you secretly enjoy wearing if nobody you knew could judge it?
We're asked to lead a street parade, but nobody knows the dance. Who pretends to be the choreographer?
Building a colourful festival float or inventing an absurd marching-band routine?
Tell me about a public celebration where the crowd became more entertaining than the programme.
At every festival, someone becomes fascinated by the food stalls and forgets why they came.
The friend who insists they know the song should be required to sing the second verse.
Which friend would find the quietest corner of a festival and return with the best stories?
Our group enters a costume contest and learns the theme changed yesterday. What's our explanation?
A dance-off between neighbouring streets or a competition for the most creative homemade banner?
Have you ever enjoyed an event far more because the people around you were having fun?
If our group wrote anonymous restaurant reviews, whose comments would give us away immediately?
We are food critics reviewing our own cooking. Who refuses to award anything above three stars?
Judging a restaurant by its chips or by the way it serves a simple glass of water?
The most dramatic food critic in a friend group is often the person who eats everything anyway.
Everyone has a different definition of what counts as 'not too spicy'.
Tell me about a meal that went from disaster to excellent because somebody improvised.
Which one of us would spend fifteen minutes describing the texture of a single biscuit?
We open a restaurant where every dish must be named after a friend. What appears on the menu?
A blind comparison of supermarket snacks or a competition to invent the best sandwich combination?
Friends should be banned from saying 'I'm not hungry' immediately before eating someone else's dessert.
We find an old map with three crosses on it. Who decides it absolutely must lead to treasure?
Which friend would follow a mysterious clue even after finding out it's probably an advertisement?
Searching for unusual street names or collecting photographs of funny shop signs?
People doing a scavenger hunt look suspicious even when they're doing nothing more than counting doors.
An excellent treasure hunt includes at least one clue that sends everybody confidently in the wrong direction.
Tell me about accidentally finding something useful while searching for something completely unrelated.
If you hid a prize somewhere in your neighbourhood, what ordinary place would be a clever choice?
Our group has to locate a red umbrella somewhere in a crowded park. What is the first strategy?
Following a series of handwritten clues or solving riddles sent by voice message?
The person who claims every puzzle is obvious should explain their answers before seeing the solution.
If our friend group made history textbooks, which minor event would receive an entire chapter?
An archaeologist from the future finds our group chat. What false conclusion would they draw about civilisation?
Having a tiny statue made in your honour or having a bus stop named after your funniest mistake?
Every group has an argument whose origin becomes harder to remember than the argument itself.
Future historians would never understand the importance of a screenshot with no context.
Tell me about a small incident your friends now refer to as though it were a historic event.
Which friend would insist on correcting every date in our imaginary museum catalogue?
Our friendship timeline must include one major turning point. What harmless event gets nominated?
Writing our history in exaggerated medieval language or drawing it as a chaotic comic strip?
The funniest memoir is one where the person being described is allowed to write footnotes.
Which friend starts explaining how to do something after watching one thirty-second tutorial?
You have five minutes to teach the group how to fold a paper plane. Who somehow creates a paper hat?
Learning to whistle with two fingers or finding out how to spin a basketball?
The best teacher among friends is the one who admits when they cannot do the thing either.
Tell me about a lesson that accidentally became a comedy routine.
Everybody listens carefully until the teacher says 'the rest is simple'.
What very specific skill would you love to demonstrate with a ridiculous amount of confidence?
Our friend volunteers to teach origami and loses the instructions halfway through. What animal do we say we made?
Trying a beginners' salsa step together or learning to tie an unusually fancy knot?
Have you ever successfully taught someone a skill you only learned that morning?
We each get to name one street in an imaginary town. Which friend chooses something deeply embarrassing?
What business should every friendly neighbourhood have, even if it makes almost no profit?
A town with a public hammock park or a town with free board games at every café?
If friends design a town together, they will argue about the location of the bakery before the hospital.
The person who loves maps will take the fictional town planning far more seriously than anyone expected.
Tell me about a place that looked so unusual you wondered whether somebody had invented it for a story.
Which friend should be banned from designing the road signs in our imaginary town?
Our fictional town elects a mascot, but the candidates are a goose and a very angry tortoise. Who wins?
A free outdoor cinema in the town square or a library open all night?
Our town council would spend its entire first meeting debating what to call the council.
Which friend would become friends with the driver before we'd even left the bus station?
Our group has to travel across town using only transport none of us has ever tried. What happens first?
Riding an old-fashioned tram for fun or trying a water taxi with absolutely no destination in mind?
Tell me about the strangest conversation you've overheard on public transport.
Someone on every long journey announces they do not need the bathroom ten minutes before the next stop.
The friend carrying snacks on public transport has more influence than the person holding the tickets.
Who would treat an airport moving walkway as a competitive sporting event?
We all board a train, but the carriage is silent and one friend starts humming the wrong tune. Who joins in?
Watching scenery change during a train journey or inventing backstories for unusual station names?
What's the funniest thing a friend has forgotten to pack for a very short journey?
What everyday annoyance deserves a completely unnecessary machine to solve it?
Our group is inventing a robot whose only job is finding missing socks. Which feature causes chaos?
A self-folding umbrella that sometimes sings or a lunchbox that loudly announces when it's opened?
Half the inventions we dream up with friends would be more complicated than the problems they solve.
Someone always volunteers to name the invention before anybody agrees what it does.
Tell me about a clever-looking gadget that failed spectacularly when somebody demonstrated it.
Which friend could convince strangers to invest in a machine that compliments houseplants?
The prototype of our automatic pancake flipper launches breakfast across the room. Who takes responsibility?
Inventing a device to stop people misplacing keys or one that reminds you why you entered a room?
The best joke inventions still need serious-looking diagrams and completely unnecessary technical terms.
Which boring daily task deserves a glamorous annual awards ceremony?
Our group has to give an emotional acceptance speech for successfully finding a parking spot. Who cries first?
A trophy for the neatest packed lunch or one for surviving the most confusing supermarket checkout?
The most ordinary chore can become dramatic when somebody insists on announcing every step.
Being the first person to change an empty toilet roll deserves applause in some households.
Tell me about an ordinary task you celebrated because it had been annoying you for months.
Which friend would create a standing ovation after someone finally returned a borrowed charger?
We're hosting an award show for the best excuse for being five minutes late. Who wins?
A medal for perfectly peeling an orange or one for opening a stubborn jar without help?
An award ceremony for everyday survival should be hosted by the most dramatic friend available.
